disagreements.their_reason: The benefit could disappear on the exact paired subset successfully edited in both arms; aggregate matrices do not establish that the compared cases are identical.
On the same 3-hop questions, zero-shot accuracy could trail trained accuracy by over 0.15; the evidence compares different populations of 609 and 77 questions.
At fixed maximum cosine, refusal could still vary materially with option count; the confusable arm already falls from 0.8485 to 0.7758 as count rises.
The gap could resume shrinking beyond 18 aliases; no measurements beyond 18 rule out continued supply-driven convergence, so the residual is not established as capability.
Verification quorum flagging any claim or overlapping attack would falsify it; claim 12 has verification votes from two quorum raters and is also attack-flagged.

0.reason: A changed basis, coordinate, or head fingerprint would falsify it; all three remain byte-identical after a nontrivial append.

1.reason: A larger depth-1 entity penalty than relation penalty, or depth-2 penalty below 0.10, would falsify it; measured penalties rule both out.

2.reason: Any refused question remaining refused or becoming wrong would falsify the conditional 432/432 claim; the transition matrix records none.

3.reason: Staleness exceeding refusal or other wrong answers would falsify it; old->old is 1 versus 150 refusals and 82 other answers.

4.reason: The benefit could disappear on the exact paired subset successfully edited in both arms; aggregate matrices do not establish that the compared cases are identical.

5.reason: A depth-2 held-pair gap beyond 0.02 would falsify the scoped parity claim; the measured gap is +0.011.

6.reason: Store-filtered exhaustive planning failing to match the walker, or model-only planning matching it, would falsify the one-corpus claim; neither occurs.

7.reason: On the same 3-hop questions, zero-shot accuracy could trail trained accuracy by over 0.15; the evidence compares different populations of 609 and 77 questions.

8.reason: Higher wrongness at either depth or refusal gain smaller than correct-answer loss would falsify it; both depth wrong-rates fall and the refusal gain dominates.

9.reason: At fixed maximum cosine, refusal could still vary materially with option count; the confusable arm already falls from 0.8485 to 0.7758 as count rises.

10.reason: A wrongness increase comparable to the novel-answering gain, or restored refusal under matched coverage, would falsify it; measured costs are far smaller and refusal still collapses.

11.reason: The gap could resume shrinking beyond 18 aliases; no measurements beyond 18 rule out continued supply-driven convergence, so the residual is not established as capability.

12.reason: Verification quorum flagging any claim or overlapping attack would falsify it; claim 12 has verification votes from two quorum raters and is also attack-flagged.

13.reason: A head gap above 0.05 on any stated population would falsify the scoped claim; all three measured gaps remain below that threshold while retrieval drops sharply.
